title: Borrow Checker: Ownership and Borrowing Rules in Runtime Python
description: Owned tracks alive, shared, and mutably_borrowed state. The rules: many readers OR one writer never both. Rust does these checks at compile time.

steps.description: Owned holds a value with three flags: alive (not moved), shared (reader count), and mutably_borrowed (exclusive writer).
move invalidates the source and returns a new Owned with the same value. It fails if already moved or borrowed.
borrow increments shared and returns the value. It fails if moved or mutably borrowed.
borrow_mut sets mutably_borrowed and returns the value. It fails if moved or any borrow is outstanding.
release decrements shared or clears mutably_borrowed to end a borrow.
attempt runs a function and prints ok with the result or REJECTED with the error.
Allowed operations: borrow twice for two readers, and move then use the new owner.

steps.question: What happens when we attempt to use after move

steps.description: Rejected operations: use after move, mutable borrow while shared, second mutable borrow, and move while borrowed.
Running prints the allowed cases as ok and the rejected cases with their error messages.
